questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 13 cm and a height of 4 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 13 × 4 = 26 cm². Say the ½ out loud before multiplying so you never skip the halving step.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a sealed container, 28g of reactants react completely. What is the mass of the products?
questions.why: 28g — mass is conserved in a closed system, so the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Name one sign that shows a chemical reaction has happened.
questions.why: Signs include a colour change, gas bubbles, a precipitate forming, or a temperature change — these show a new substance has been made.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: Why do supermarkets place sugary snacks near the checkout?
questions.answer: To tempt shoppers waiting in line
questions.why: Checkout placement is a deliberate marketing trick — bored, waiting shoppers grab snacks on impulse. Kids sometimes think it's just shelf organisation, but it's placed there specifically to trigger unplanned buying.
options: To tempt shoppers waiting in line
To show the snacks are fresher there
To keep the queue area tidy
To group items by their price

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, which nutrient is usually listed under 'carbohydrates'?
questions.why: Sugar is a type of carbohydrate, so labels list it as a sub-item under the carbohydrate total — it's often mistaken for its own separate category.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What gas is often seen as bubbles when a chemical reaction happens?
questions.why: Bubbling shows a gas is being produced, one of the clear signs a chemical reaction has taken place.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: Why do nutrition labels list 'per serving' alongside 'per 100g'?
questions.answer: It shows a realistic single portion
questions.why: The 'per serving' column estimates what one actual helping contains, helping you judge real intake. Some assume it covers the whole pack or only tracks sugar, but it's a portion-based figure for all nutrients.
options: It shows a realistic single portion
It shows the cheapest portion size
It shows the total package weight
It shows only the sugar content
